Payments Vision 2028 RBI has been periodically preparing Payments Vision since 2001. This includes providing strategic direction for structured development of the payment and settlement systems in India. RBI has released ‘Payments Vision 2028’ for the duration up to December 2028. It has been prepared after considering inputs from various stakeholders. It consists of 15 specific initiatives which are to be taken up during the course of next three years. Payments Vision 2028 core theme – ‘Shaping India’s Payment Frontier’. It underscores the dual imperative of consolidating and strengthening the existing systems / infrastructure, while pioneering the future of payments.

# Page 4^page=4


# Page 5^page=5
Specific Initiatives Facility for the remitter to enable / disable transactions on any digital payment mode through issuer channels Customers can already Switch on\ off domestic & international card transactions, giving better control over usage Proposal to extend this feature to all digital payment modes (UPI, wallets, net banking, etc.). Contribute towards controlling frauds in digital payment transactions. RBI shall publish regular reports on cross-border payments Covering key metrics: volumes, costs, transparency, speed, performance of various channels Track global developments in legal, regulatory, technological, and process advancements Benchmarking India’s progress against global trends the reports shall also Identify gaps and areas for improvement Assesses impact of international dev on India’s payment system Reports on Cross-Border Payments: Domestic trends, global developments, and strategic implications for India’s payment ecosystem

# Page 6^page=6
Specific Initiatives Streamline cross- border payment authorisation under PSS Act, 2007 and FEMA, 1999 In order to facilitate cross-border transfer of funds, entities need to seek authorisation under the PSS Act, 2007 and an authorised person license under FEMA, 1999. To improve efficiency, a single-window application process shall be considered. This will allow firms to enter the market faster and at lower cost instead of navigating multiple approvals - enhancing EoDB Cross-border payments are vital for India’s trade and remittances. Efficient payments are critical for reducing the remittance cost, but these payments are complex due to multiple intermediaries, jurisdictions and regulations. The global agenda, shaped by the G20, also aims to make these payments faster, cheaper, more transparent, and accessible. RBI is actively improving the cross- border payments ecosystem through regulatory liberalisation and technological initiatives. RBI shall undertake a comprehensive review of the existing ecosystem to identify frictions from regulatory, operational, and technological perspective to strengthen India’s cross-border payment landscape, promote innovation and competition, and align with global best practices. Review of cross-border payments ecosystem with an objective to increase efficiency of cross-border payments

# Page 7^page=7
Specific Initiatives Limiting liability of customers – Shared Responsibility Framework The existing Limiting Liability Framework for safeguarding customers from payment frauds places responsibility and liability exclusively on the issuer bank. A shared responsibility model is proposed, where both issuer and beneficiary banks share liability for unauthorised digital transactions, encouraging better fraud prevention, coordination, and stronger consumer protection. To encourage innovation, a new class of Small Payment System Providers (SPSPs) is proposed allowing them to operate without prior authorisation at early stages. Regulation would be applied later based on their scale and risk profile. This risk-based approach promotes ease of doing business while maintaining systemic stability. Recognise Small Payment System Providers – Perpetual Regulatory Sandbox

# Page 8^page=8
Specific Initiatives Develop Payments Research and Training Capacity The global payments landscape rapidly evolves with new and emerging technologies. To keep pace with evolving payment technologies, it is proposed to enhance research and training in areas like policy making, risk management, fraud prevention, cross border payments, cybersecurity etc. while building global and domestic partnerships with various central banks, international standard setting bodies, other countries especially from the Global South, for knowledge sharing. Cyber KRI framework for non-bank PSOs shall be developed and implemented. This framework shall assess and monitor robustness in cyber security of such entities on a continuous basis. It shall enable RBI to systematically identify and monitor key risk indicators across the industry, compare the cyber resilience of different entities, track their security posture over time as also provide early warning signals to identify and monitor potential IT and cyber risks. Cyber Key Risk Indicators (KRI) framework for non-bank Payment System Operators (PSOs)

# Page 9^page=9
Specific Initiatives Review of design and security features of cheques and explore introduction of electronic cheques Building on the existing CTS-2010 standards, banks have independently implemented additional security features, leading to variations across the system. A comprehensive review of the design and security features of cheques shall be undertaken to enhance uniformity, strengthen fraud prevention, and ensure alignment with emerging processes. The review shall identify and adopt best practices. Further introduction of electronic cheques in India shall be explored. With rapid growth in digital payments ecosystem, it is proposed to create an AI- enabled, user-friendly payments database, improving transparency, monitoring, and supporting data-driven innovation. This shall also serve as a single point of access for cross border payments data which shall provide a unified and dynamic view of India's cross border payments ecosystem Facilitate enhanced access to payments data

# Page 10^page=10
Specific Initiatives Customers face challenges in managing their payment instructions in case their account number changes due to shifting to another bank, merger of banks, etc. To address this, feasibility of implementing a ‘Payments Switching Service’ shall be explored. It is envisaged as a centralised service that would facilitate migration of payment instructions, both incoming and outgoing, from one account to another, thereby enabling customers to change their bank accounts with minimal friction. Using this functionality, customers shall be able to view all payment flows linked to their accounts and initiate either a full or partial switch with appropriate authorisation. The objective is to provide customers with centralised control over their payment instructions, facilitate orderly transitions during systemic changes like bank mergers. Payments Switching Service (PaSS)

# Page 11^page=11
Specific Initiatives With rapid growth in digital payments, many new players are involved— fintech firms, payment apps, etc. These entities are no longer just facilitators; they play a critical role in executing and managing transactions. Large e-commerce platforms and payment intermediaries now: Handle huge volumes of transactions, Store customer data and Control payment flows. These aspects shall be examined in detail and, if required, the scope of direct regulations shall be extended to cover such entities. On similar lines, the case for introducing white label solutions in Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS) and bringing such Assisted payment providers (like BCs, agents) within the regulatory fold would be explored Bringing entities playing critical role in payments ecosystem within the regulatory ambit

# Page 12^page=12
Specific Initiatives A unique identifier for non-individuals that would enable identification of parties to a transaction is crucial for managing risks in the financial system. In this regard, the feasibility of implementing a uniform Domestic Legal Entity Identifier (DLEI) shall be studied. Currently, there exist myriad identifiers in India, each with its own specific purpose and features. The DLEI, if found feasible, could be new or selected from the existing identifiers. Implementing a uniform Domestic Legal Entity Identifier (DLEI) Reimagine card payments in India It is proposed to build an open and interoperable card ecosystem to promote competition and innovation, enhance security through tokenisation, and ensure greater choice and transparent pricing for users.

# Page 14^page=14
With reference to the initiatives proposed by the Reserve Bank of India under its Payments Vision, consider the following statements: 1. The proposed facility to enable/disable digital payment modes extends the existing card-based control features to all forms of digital payments, aiming to enhance user control and fraud prevention. 2. The Payments Switching Service (PaSS) is envisaged as a decentralised mechanism that allows banks to independently migrate customer payment instructions without requiring customer authorisation. 3. The Shared Responsibility Framework proposes that liability for unauthorised transactions will be jointly borne by both the issuer bank and the beneficiary bank, instead of being solely on the issuer. 4. The proposal for Small Payment System Providers (SPSPs) suggests that such entities would be allowed to operate initially without prior authorisation, and be brought under regulation once they reach systemic significance. 5. The Domestic Legal Entity Identifier (DLEI) aims to replace all existing identifiers in India with a single mandatory identifier exclusively for cross-border transactions. Which of the statements given above are correct? A. 1, 3 and 4 only B. 1, 2 and 5 only C. 2, 3, 4 and 5 only D. 1, 3, 4 and 5 only E. 1, 2, 3 and 4 only MCQs for Practice
